summary: Source decomposition from four primary sources read directly: Rodrigues Jacinto-Williams Appendix B (printed pp. 79-81), Pollack-Stevens 'Critical slope p-adic L-functions' (Sections 1, 2, 3.1-3.2, 8 and 9), Bellaiche 'Critical p-adic L-functions' (Sections 1.1-1.4), and Amice-Velu (Theoreme III, printed p. 125). Formulas (2) of Pollack-Stevens and (4)-(5) of Bellaiche were read from rendered page images at 220 and 500 dpi because the PDF text layers scramble the fractions and drop a bar on Q-bar_p. TWO PRINTED DISCREPANCIES ARE RECORDED. (1) Pollack-Stevens equation (2) prints L(f, chi^{-1}, 1) as the interpolated value, but its left-hand side depends on j and no other factor supplies that dependence; Bellaiche, restating the same Pollack-Stevens interpolation property, prints L_infinity(f phi^{-1}, j+1), which fixes the reading. (2) Bellaiche's modification factor (5) prints alpha in BOTH Euler-factor denominators while its prefactor is 1/beta^nu and the refinement being interpolated is f_beta with U_p f_beta = beta f_beta; by Bellaiche's own Sec. 1.3 the denominators should be beta. The reconciliation of RJW Theorem B.1 (one Euler factor, f of level divisible by p) with Bellaiche (4)-(5) (two Euler factors, newform of level prime to p plus a chosen refinement) is exactly the second-Euler-factor point the stage names, and the Gauss-sum/2-pi-i dictionary between the two printed normalizations is recorded as an AUTHORED computation still to be verified. Three further hypotheses are carried explicitly: the modular-symbol comparison H^1_c = Hom_{Gamma_0}(Delta_0, -) needs the order of every torsion element of Gamma_0 to act invertibly; the control theorem needs slope STRICTLY less than k+1; and at critical slope a (k+1)-admissible distribution is NOT determined by its interpolation values, with Pollack-Stevens stating that their method does not give the missing values at x^{k+1}chi and Bellaiche stating (Theorem 2, whose proof is in his Sec. 4 and was not read) that at a theta-critical point ALL the interpolation values vanish except in one Eisenstein case. All five stages are partial; no canonical integral period and no integrality statement for the measure was found in any source read (Amice-Velu p. 120 quote Manin's level-one statement that D^k Q_k^epsilon(x) is an algebraic integer, which is neither). [Corrected in review REVIEW-EXT-08-EXT-16: RJW Theorem B.1 was re-read from a render of printed p. 80. It prints chi-bar in both L-values; the PDF text layer drops the bar. So RJW and Pollack-Stevens interpolate the SAME chi^{-1}-twisted value. They differ in the placement of the Gauss sum, the overall sign, the power of 2 pi i and the Euler factor at n = 0. Two further printed tensions are now recorded. First, Pollack-Stevens (2) and Amice-Velu Theoreme III(a) print no Euler factor at n = 0, where RJW print (1 - p^j/alpha_p). Second, Bellaiche (4) prints the parity condition phi(-1) = pm 1, whereas his own p. 7 support statement and Amice-Velu (1) select the sign by phi(-1)(-1)^j. The control theorem is proved in Pollack-Stevens Sec. 5, contrary to the earlier text. The unsupported link from PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L3 was removed.]

nodes.title: Delta_0-valued modular symbols and the comparison with H^1_c, with the torsion hypothesis
nodes.statement: Let p be a prime, N prime to p, Gamma_0 = Gamma_1(N) intersect Gamma_0(p), and S_0(p) the semigroup of integral matrices (a b; c d) with p not dividing a, p dividing c and ad - bc nonzero. For a right Z[S_0(p)]-module M let M-tilde be the associated locally constant sheaf on the open modular curve Y_{Gamma_0}, and H^1_c(Gamma_0, M) = H^1_c(Y_{Gamma_0}, M-tilde). Set Delta_0 = Div^0(P^1(Q)) with its left GL_2(Q)-action by linear fractional transformations, and let S_0(p) act on the right on Hom(Delta_0, M) by (phi | gamma)(D) = phi(gamma D) | gamma. THEN, PROVIDED THE ORDER OF EVERY TORSION ELEMENT OF Gamma_0 ACTS INVERTIBLY ON M, there is a canonical Hecke-equivariant isomorphism H^1_c(Gamma_0, M) = Hom_{Gamma_0}(Delta_0, M). The U_p operator is realized explicitly by phi | U_p = sum over a = 0 to p-1 of phi | (1 a; 0 p).
hypotheses: The comparison is CONDITIONAL on the order of each torsion element of Gamma_0 acting invertibly on M. Pollack-Stevens list the sufficient conditions: N at least 4, or M a vector space over a field of characteristic 0, or Gamma_0 torsion-free, or M a Z_p-module with p > 3. This is exactly the elliptic-stabilizer point the stage insists on
M must be a right Z[S_0(p)]-module, not merely a Gamma_0-module; the U_p formula uses matrices of determinant p that lie in S_0(p) but not in Gamma_0
The Hecke algebra H is the free polynomial algebra over Z on T_l for l not dividing Np and U_q for q dividing Np
The involution comes from iota = (-1 0; 0 1), which normalizes Gamma_0; the decomposition into plus and minus eigenspaces requires 2 to act invertibly on M

Determinant twists: for r in Z_{>=0}, M(r) is M with the S_0(p)-action twisted by the r-th power of the determinant, and H^1_c(M(r)) = H^1_c(M)(r), where T_l acts by l^r T_l and U_q by q^r U_q. Pollack-Stevens Sec. 2.2 state this for nonnegative r and call it tautological.
proofSteps: Form the local system M-tilde on Y_{Gamma_0} and its compactly supported cohomology.
Under the torsion hypothesis, quote the canonical isomorphism with Gamma_0-equivariant homomorphisms on degree-zero divisors ([2, Prop. 4.2] in Pollack-Stevens's numbering, i.e. Ash-Stevens).
Check Hecke equivariance and record the explicit U_p formula.
Record the determinant twist and the involution with their separate hypotheses.
acceptance: For N < 4, p = 2 or 3 and M a Z_p-module, determine whether Gamma_0 has torsion whose order is divisible by p. Where it does, check that the identification (1) is not available without a torsion-free auxiliary level and descent. [Reworded in review: the source gives only sufficient conditions, so failure is not automatic.]
Verify the U_p formula against the q-expansion action on a weight-two symbol
Check H^1_c(M(r)) = H^1_c(M)(r) on a concrete twist

nodes.title: The interpolation formula for the analytic p-adic L-function, in two printed normalizations
nodes.statement: Let f be a cuspidal Hecke eigenform of weight k+2. Two printed normalizations of the same interpolation property are recorded. (RJW, level Gamma_0(N) with p dividing N, alpha_p the U_p eigenvalue, v_p(alpha_p) < k+1): for every Dirichlet character chi of conductor p^n and every 0 <= j <= k, L_p^an(f, chi-bar, j+1), defined as the integral of chi(x)x^j against L_p^an(f), equals -alpha_p^{-n} (1 - chi(p)p^j/alpha_p) G(chi) j! p^{nj} (2 pi i)^{-(j+1)} L(f, chi-bar, j+1)/Omega_f^{pm}. (Pollack-Stevens, level Gamma_0 = Gamma_1(N) cap Gamma_0(p), slope h < k+1): mu_f(x^j chi) = a_p^{-n} p^{n(j+1)} (-2 pi i)^{-j} j! tau(chi^{-1})^{-1} L(f, chi^{-1}, 1)/Omega_f^{pm}. Both formulas interpolate the chi^{-1}-twisted L-value, since chi-bar = chi^{-1}. They are NOT literally equal, and differ in four ways. First, G(chi) multiplies in RJW while tau(chi^{-1}) divides in Pollack-Stevens (with p^{nj} against p^{n(j+1)}). Second, RJW carry an overall minus sign. Third, the powers of 2 pi i differ. Fourth, RJW print the Euler factor and Pollack-Stevens do not. For n >= 1 that factor is 1 because chi(p) = 0, so beyond constants the printed formulas disagree only at n = 0. The printed last argument '1' of the Pollack-Stevens L-value is inconsistent with the j-dependence of both sides. Bellaiche, restating the same Pollack-Stevens interpolation property, prints L_infinity(f phi^{-1}, j+1), which is the reading under which the formula is consistent. [Corrected in review: the RJW formula prints chi-bar in both L-values. The bars are visible on a render of printed p. 80, but the PDF text layer drops them, so the earlier claim that the two normalizations differ in the twist was wrong.]
hypotheses: RJW: f has level Gamma_0(N) with p DIVIDING N, so L(f,s) is the L-function of the p-level form and carries only one Euler factor at p
RJW: the hypothesis is v_p(alpha_p) < k+1; the theorem does NOT cover v_p(alpha_p) = k+1, and RJW say so explicitly

Pollack-Stevens: chi is a finite order character of Z_p^x of conductor p^n. For n >= 1, chi(p) = 0 and RJW's Euler factor is 1. For n = 0 (chi trivial), RJW print the factor (1 - p^j/alpha_p) while Pollack-Stevens (2) prints none. Amice-Velu Theoreme III(a) likewise shows none, on its own domain X(Z*_Delta). The printed formulas therefore genuinely disagree at n = 0, not only by normalization constants. REVIEWER COMPUTATION, not a source statement: Pollack-Stevens p. 5 give phi | U_p = sum_a phi | (1 a; 0 p), and by Sec. 3.3 the matrix (1 a; 0 p) acts on test functions by g -> g(a + pz). Hence an eigensymbol with Phi | U_p = alpha Phi satisfies Phi({inf}-{0})(1_{pZ_p} z^j) = (p^j/alpha) Phi({inf}-{0})(z^j). Restricting to Z_p^x therefore multiplies the moment by (1 - p^j/alpha), which supports RJW's factor. [Corrected in review.]

Both period normalizations Omega_f^{pm} are defined only up to a scalar: the plus/minus eigensymbols are normalized by a CHOICE (Pollack-Stevens normalize phi^{pm}_f to have size 1; Bellaiche says the formula holds 'up to a scalar independent on phi t^j')

The sign is selected by parity. Bellaiche's (4) PRINTS the condition as phi(-1) = pm 1. But his own p. 7 statement is that L^pm(f_beta, sigma) = 0 whenever sigma(-1) is not pm 1, and for sigma = phi t^j that means phi(-1)(-1)^j = pm 1. Amice-Velu (1) (printed p. 120) likewise attach the period omega_{(-1)^k chi(-1)}. The two readings agree only for even j. [Corrected in review: the earlier text took the printed phi(-1) = pm 1 at face value.]

RJW define G(chi) only for primitive chi of conductor p^n with n >= 1 (Definition 5.2, printed p. 29). At n = 0 the value G(chi) = 1 is a convention that the statement of Theorem B.1 needs but RJW do not state. [Added in review.]

Amice-Velu's uniqueness in Theoreme III is relative to condition (b), G_lambda = o(Log^{w+1}), not to growth of order v_p(lambda). The finer bound o(Log^{h+1}) with h = [v_p(lambda)] is the separate conclusion (c). [Added in review.]
proofSteps: Record RJW Theorem B.1 verbatim, with its growth clause (order v_p(alpha_p)) and its uniqueness clause.
Record Pollack-Stevens formula (2) verbatim from the page image.
Record Bellaiche formula (4) with its modification factor (5), which is the same interpolation property for a newform of level Gamma_1(N) with p prime to N and a chosen refinement.

AUTHORED RECONCILIATION (not quoted from any source). For chi primitive of conductor p^n with n >= 1, RJW Remark 5.3(i) gives G(chi) G(chi^{-1}) = chi(-1) p^n. If Pollack-Stevens' tau is the same Gauss sum (they say only 'a Gauss sum'), then p^{n(j+1)}/tau(chi^{-1}) = chi(-1) G(chi) p^{nj}. Reading the L-argument as j+1, the Pollack-Stevens value divided by the RJW value is then -chi(-1)(-1)^j (2 pi i) times Omega_RJW^pm/Omega_PS^pm. The factor -chi(-1)(-1)^j (2 pi i) is constant on each parity class chi(-1)(-1)^j = pm 1. It can therefore be absorbed into the choice of Omega_f^pm exactly when the sign pm is indexed by chi(-1)(-1)^j. At n = 0 the Euler-factor disagreement is not a normalization constant and is not absorbed. This is the 'dictionary' the stage asks to prove; it is recorded here as a computation to be verified, not as a source statement. [Corrected in review: the earlier version omitted the sign (-1)^j coming from (-2 pi i)^j and RJW's overall minus sign, and did not note the n = 0 discrepancy.]
acceptance: Check the n = 0 case of RJW Theorem B.1 separately. There G(chi) = 1 by convention, alpha_p^{-n} = 1, and the Euler factor 1 - p^j/alpha_p is the only surviving modification. Decide between RJW (factor present) and the printed Pollack-Stevens (2) (factor absent), using the U_p-eigen relation.
Check that for n >= 1 the Euler factor is 1 because chi(p) = 0, so that the two printed formulas differ only in the placement of the Gauss sum, the overall sign and the (2 pi i) conventions.

Check that Pollack-Stevens' tau agrees with RJW's G (Definition 5.2). Then verify G(chi) G(chi^{-1}) = chi(-1) p^n (RJW Remark 5.3(i)) for chi primitive of conductor p^n, and confirm the reconciliation above, including the residual factor -chi(-1)(-1)^j (2 pi i).
Verify that the printed Pollack-Stevens L-argument must be j+1 by checking both sides at two different values of j
Check the parity convention on one odd j: L^pm(f_beta, phi t^j) must vanish unless phi(-1)(-1)^j = pm 1. [Added in review.]

nodes.title: The two refinements of a newform and the modification factor with both Euler factors
nodes.statement:
Let f be a newform of weight k+2 and level Gamma_1(N) with p prime to N, T_p f = a_p f and

f = epsilon(p) f. Let alpha, beta be the roots of X^2 - a_p X + epsilon(p) p^{k+1} (assumed distinct). The two refinements are f_alpha(z) = f(z) - beta f(pz) and f_beta(z) = f(z) - alpha f(pz); they are the two normalized forms of level Gamma = Gamma_1(N) cap Gamma_0(p) that have the same T_l (l prime to pN) and diamond eigenvalues as f AND are U_p-eigenforms [the U_p-eigenform condition was restored in review; without it the space of such normalized forms is not two points], and they satisfy U_p f_beta = beta f_beta and U_p f_alpha = alpha f_alpha. A REFINEMENT IS THE CHOICE OF A ROOT, not a property of f. For a refinement the interpolation factor is e_p(beta, phi t^j) = beta^{-nu} (1 - phi-bar(p) epsilon(p) p^{k-j}/D)(1 - phi(p) p^j/D), where the conductor of phi is m = p^nu M with M prime to p, and D is the U_p eigenvalue of the chosen refinement. Bellaiche PRINTS alpha in both denominators of e_p(beta, -); D = beta is the reading supported by his Sec. 1.3 and by the reviewer computation recorded in the gaps; TWO Euler factors appear, because the L-function on the right is that of the level-prime-to-p NEWFORM f, not of the refinement.
hypotheses: p prime to N; alpha not equal to beta is assumed 'without loss of generality and for simplicity' by Bellaiche
Bellaiche also assumes throughout that p is ODD
When phi is ramified at p (nu >= 1) both Euler factors are 1 because phi(p) = phi-bar(p) = 0, and e_p reduces to beta^{-nu}; the Euler factors are visible only for phi unramified at p

PRINTED DISCREPANCY: Bellaiche's formula (5) prints alpha in BOTH Euler-factor denominators while the prefactor is 1/beta^nu and the L-function attached is that of the refinement f_beta with U_p f_beta = beta f_beta. Since alpha and beta are defined as the two distinct roots and beta is the eigenvalue of the refinement in question, the denominators should be beta. This is recorded as a printed inconsistency in the source, verified against Bellaiche's own Sec. 1.3 definitions. REVIEWER COMPUTATION (not a source statement): f_beta(z) = f(z) - alpha f(pz) gives L(f_beta, phi-bar, s) = (1 - phi-bar(p) alpha p^{-s}) L(f, phi-bar, s). At s = j+1, alpha p^{-(j+1)} = epsilon(p) p^{k-j}/beta because alpha beta = epsilon(p) p^{k+1}. The U_p-eigen relation with eigenvalue beta gives the second factor (1 - phi(p) p^j/beta) at unramified phi. Both denominators are therefore beta, matching the prefactor 1/beta^nu. For weight two (k = j = 0, epsilon(p) = 1) and trivial character, the same computation gives (1 - 1/alpha)^2 for the alpha-refinement.

nodes.title: The specialization map is an isomorphism on the slope < k+1 subspace
nodes.statement: Let D_k be the space of locally Q_p-analytic distributions on Z_p with the weight-k action of Gamma_0, and Sym^k(Q_p^2) its finite-dimensional quotient. The induced Hecke-equivariant specialization map H^1_c(Gamma_0, D_k) -> H^1_c(Gamma_0, Sym^k(Q_p^2)) restricts to an ISOMORPHISM on the subspace where U_p acts with slope STRICTLY LESS THAN k+1. Consequently a slope-h eigensymbol phi_f with h < k+1 lifts uniquely to a Hecke-eigensymbol Phi_f, and integrating Phi_f over the divisor {infinity} - {0} and restricting to Z_p^x gives the p-adic L-function mu_f.
hypotheses: The strict inequality h < k+1 is essential; the theorem fails at slope exactly k+1, which is the whole point of the critical-slope work

The source of the isomorphism is the identification of the kernel of specialization with H^1_c(Gamma_0, D_{-2-k})(k+1), a twist by the (k+1)-st power of the determinant, on which U_p acts with slope at least k+1

The surjectivity on the slope-< k+1 part comes from two inputs: surjectivity before slope decomposition (Lemma 5.1, whose proof computes H^2_c(Gamma_0, D-dagger_{-2-k}) = 0 in Lemma 5.2), and exactness of passing to slope parts (Proposition 4.8). Proposition 4.8 rests on the Riesz-type splitting X = X(Q) + X'(Q) in the category C of Sec. 4 (printed pp. 9-11; only p. 11 was read). [Corrected in review.]

Pollack-Stevens attribute the theorem to Stevens ([19] and [15, Thm. 5.12]) and give a proof, which they call a sketch, in Sec. 5.2 (Theorem 5.4, printed pp. 13-14). Lemma 5.1 gives the exact sequence 0 -> H^1_c(D-dagger_{-2-k})(k+1) -> H^1_c(D-dagger_k) -> H^1_c(P_k^dual) -> 0. Proposition 4.8 and Lemma 5.3 pass to slope < k+1 parts. U_p has norm <= p^{-(k+1)} on the twisted kernel, so Lemma 4.9(2) kills its slope < k+1 part. [Corrected in review: the earlier text said the proof is not reproduced in this paper; the packet had not read Sec. 5.]

nodes.title: Pollack-Stevens: specialization is an isomorphism on the f-generalized eigenspace iff f is not in the image of theta^{k+1}
nodes.statement: Let f be an eigenform in S_{k+2}(Gamma_0, Q-bar_p) of slope exactly k+1, and let theta^{k+1} : M^dagger_{-k}(Gamma, Q_p) -> M^dagger_{k+2}(Gamma, Q_p) be the p-adic theta operator acting on q-expansions by (q d/dq)^{k+1}. Then H^1_c(Gamma_0, D_k)_{(f)} -> H^1_c(Gamma_0, P_k^dual)_{(f)} is an isomorphism IF AND ONLY IF f is not in the image of theta^{k+1}, where the subscript (f) is the GENERALIZED eigenspace. When f is not in that image, the unique eigensymbol Phi_f lifting phi_f defines mu_f = Phi_f({infinity} - {0}) restricted to Z_p^x, which is (k+1)-admissible and satisfies the interpolation property; when f IS in the image, there is a nonzero eigensymbol in the kernel of specialization.
hypotheses: The slope must be exactly k+1; the theorem is about the critical-slope subspace
The subscript (f) denotes the GENERALIZED eigenspace, not the eigenspace

A (k+1)-admissible distribution is NOT determined by the interpolation property alone: Pollack-Stevens state that one would also need the values at characters x^{k+1}chi, and that their method does not give those values

A WEAKER version (Theorem 6.7, printed p. 16) is proved first, under two extra hypotheses: Gamma_0 has no elements of order p, and f has no mod p companion form. Proposition 6.9 shows that f in the image of theta^{k+1} implies f has a mod p companion form, so Theorem 8.1 implies Theorem 6.7 (Remark 8.3). The order-p hypothesis is used in Sec. 6 for the integral filtration (Lemma 6.2, where p does not act invertibly on Fil^r D^0_{-k}); Theorem 8.1 itself does not assume it. [Corrected in review: the order-p hypothesis had been omitted.]

The proof of Theorem 8.1 uses the exact sequence 0 -> H^1_c(D_{-2-k})(k+1)_{(f)} -> H^1_c(D_k)_{(f)} -> H^1_c(P_k^dual)_{(f)} -> 0 together with Theorem 7.1, which produces an overconvergent eigenform from an eigensymbol. The sequence comes from Lemma 5.1 and Proposition 4.8 on slope-(=k+1) parts, followed by Lemma 6.4. Lemma 6.4 preserves exactness for generalized eigenspaces but not for eigenspaces (Remark 6.5). Theorem 7.1 (Stevens [18, 19]) is applied only in the negative weight -2-k and at slope 0, so its E_2^crit exception does not intervene (Remark 7.5).
proofSteps: Form the exact sequence of generalized eigenspaces with kernel H^1_c(D_{-2-k})(k+1)_{(f)}: apply Proposition 4.8 to Lemma 5.1 on the slope-(=k+1) parts, then pass to f-isotypic parts with Lemma 6.4 (as in the proof of Theorem 6.7, printed p. 16).

If a nonzero H-eigensymbol Psi exists in the kernel, untwist it and apply Theorem 7.1 to get an overconvergent eigenform g in M^dagger_{-k} with the same eigenpacket; then theta^{k+1} g has the eigenpacket of f, and comparing q-expansions gives f = theta^{k+1} g.
Conversely, if f = theta^{k+1} g, Theorem 7.1 produces an eigensymbol Psi_0 for g; twisting gives a nonzero element of the kernel.

Define mu_f from the unique lift in the non-theta-critical case; admissibility is quoted from [15, Lemma 6.2] and the interpolation property is formal from Phi_f being a U_p-eigensymbol lifting phi_f.

nodes.title: Bellaiche's one-dimensionality theorem for decent refinements and the vanishing of the interpolation values in the theta-critical case
nodes.statement: Let f be a newform of weight k+2 and level Gamma_1(N) (p odd, prime to N) and f_beta a refinement of f at p. Call f_beta DECENT if (i) f is Eisenstein, or (ii) f_beta is non-critical, or (iii) f is cuspidal and H^1_g(G_Q, rho_f) = 0. Assume f_beta is decent, and if f is Eisenstein that v_p(beta) > 0. Then for both signs the eigenspace Symb^{pm}_Gamma(D_k)[f_beta] is ONE-DIMENSIONAL, and the following are equivalent: (i) f_beta is critical; (ii) the generalized eigenspaces Symb^{pm}_Gamma(D_k)_{(f_beta)} have dimension strictly greater than 1; (iii) the specialization rho_k^*(Symb^{pm}_Gamma(D_k)[f_beta]) = 0 for both signs. The L-functions are L^{pm}(f_beta, sigma) = Phi^{pm}_{f_beta}({infinity} - {0})(sigma), each defined only up to a nonzero scalar. THEOREM 2: if f_beta is theta-critical then L^{pm}(f_beta, phi t^j) = 0 for ALL finite-order phi and all 0 <= j <= k, with one exception (f Eisenstein, f_beta not critical, sign epsilon(f_beta), chi trivial and j = k). When f_beta is critical, dim Symb^{pm}(D_k)_{(f_beta)} = e > 1 equals the ramification degree of the weight map at the corresponding point of the eigencurve, which is smooth, and e-1 SECONDARY L-functions are defined by L^{pm}_i(f_beta, sigma) = (d^i L^{pm}(y,sigma)/dy^i) at y = x.
hypotheses: p ODD and prime to N throughout Bellaiche's paper
The 'decent' hypothesis is required; Bellaiche notes all CM forms are decent and that it is conjectured that every cuspidal form satisfies (iii)

The L-functions are defined only up to a nonzero scalar, since the generators Phi^{pm}_{f_beta} are; the secondary L-functions are only defined up to a scalar AND up to adding a linear combination of the earlier ones, so it is the FLAG F_0 contained in F_1 contained in ... that is well defined

Theorem 2's vanishing means the standard interpolation values do not determine the theta-critical L-function; the interpolation property (4) is recovered only by the TOP secondary L-function L^{pm}_{e-1}, while L^{pm}_i for 0 <= i <= e-2 satisfy the vanishing property (6). Bellaiche states these interpolation properties of the secondary L-functions only under the assumption that f is CUSPIDAL. [Corrected in review: the cuspidality assumption had been omitted.]
The eigencurve is NOT etale over the weight space at a critical point, which Bellaiche identifies as the new difficulty in constructing the two-variable L-function

Bellaiche's D = D[r] is the dual of the functions on Z_p that are analytic on each closed ball of radius r. He takes r = 1/p in the introduction and notes that 'nothing would change for any other value of r'. His involution iota is (1 0; 0 -1). Pollack-Stevens' D_k is D_k[1], with iota = (-1 0; 0 1). The dimension statements of Theorem 1 therefore concern Bellaiche's module and are not literally statements about the Pollack-Stevens spaces. [Added in review.]

Define L^{pm}(f_beta,sigma) as the Mellin transform of Phi^{pm}_{f_beta}({infinity} - {0}).

Theorem 2 is proved in Bellaiche Sec. 4, which was not read. Theorem 1's criterion (iii) is equivalent to f_beta being CRITICAL, not theta-critical. For f cuspidal, critical and theta-critical coincide (printed p. 5), so (TS pm) holds for both signs and the values at phi t^j with 0 <= j <= k vanish. That these values depend only on the specialization of the eigensymbol is a reviewer inference from the U_p-eigen relation, not a quoted step. For f Eisenstein, theta-critical is equivalent to critical slope and need not imply critical. Theorem 1 then gives only (TS_{-epsilon(f_beta)}); the remaining vanishing for the sign epsilon(f_beta), with its exception at trivial character and j = k, needs the Sec. 4 argument. [Corrected in review: the earlier step derived Theorem 2 from (iii) for every theta-critical f_beta, which Theorem 1 does not give.]

nodes.title: The analytic, arithmetic and algebraic p-adic L-functions of a modular form and the relations among them
nodes.statement: For f a modular form: the ANALYTIC p-adic L-function is L_p^an(f) of Theorem B.1; the ARITHMETIC one is Log_{V_f}(z_Kato(f)) where z_Kato(f) is Kato's Euler system localized at p, living in H^1_Iw(Q_p, V_f), and Log_{V_f} is Perrin-Riou's big logarithm; the ALGEBRAIC one is L_p^alg(f) = ch_{Lambda(Z_p^x)}(X_{p^infinity}(V_f)), defined when f is p-ordinary and using Kato's theorem that the Selmer module is Lambda-torsion. Kato's explicit reciprocity law gives L_p^an(f) = L_p^arith(f) in D^la(Z_p^x). The Iwasawa Main Conjecture for f, L_p^alg(f) = (L_p^an(f)) inside Lambda(Z_p^x), is a theorem of Kato and Skinner-Urban UNDER SOME MILD ADDITIONAL TECHNICAL HYPOTHESES.

gaps.title: Stage-ordering tension: L1's stated scope needs L2's refinement data

That comparison is exactly what separates RJW Theorem B.1 (f of level Gamma_0(N) with p dividing N, ONE Euler factor) from Bellaiche (4)-(5) (f a newform of level prime to p with a CHOSEN refinement, TWO Euler factors). The refinement data - the two roots alpha, beta of X^2 - a_p X + epsilon(p)p^{k+1} and the two p-stabilizations - is assigned by the atlas to stage L2, and data/atlas.json records the edge L1 -> L2 (L2 requires L1). RESOLUTION NEEDED BY THE ATLAS OWNER: either narrow L1 to the fixed-level statement and move the newform comparison to L2, or split the refinement definitions out of L2 into a prerequisite of L1. Review note (REVIEW-EXT-08-EXT-16): the roadmap summary in data/atlas.json says 'The starting form can have p in its level; the good-prime p-stabilization comparison is a separate result'. review.notes: All 7 nodes and 4 draft links were checked against the library copies; all four SHA-256 hashes match. Displayed formulas were checked on page renders: RJW p. 80, Pollack-Stevens p. 21, Bellaiche p. 8, and Amice-Velu pp. 119-120 and 125-129. The main corrections are these. (1) RJW Theorem B.1 prints chi-bar in both L-values; the text layer drops the bar. The packet's claim that RJW and Pollack-Stevens differ in the twist was therefore false, and the atlas's L1 transcription has the same error. (2) The authored Gauss-sum reconciliation omitted the signs (-1)^j and -1; the residual factor is -chi(-1)(-1)^j (2 pi i), which is absorbable into the periods only when the sign is indexed by chi(-1)(-1)^j. (3) At n = 0 the printed sources disagree on the Euler factor: RJW print it, while Pollack-Stevens (2) and Amice-Velu III(a) do not. A reviewer computation from the U_p-eigen relation supports RJW. (7) Bellaiche's Theorem 1(iii) characterizes CRITICAL, not theta-critical, refinements, so the derivation of Theorem 2 was wrong for Eisenstein series; the secondary interpolation properties assume f cuspidal. (8) The refinements need the U_p-eigenform condition. (9) The Amice-Velu domain is X(Z*_Delta). (10) Amice-Velu p. 120 does state Manin's algebraicity theorem. (11) Bellaiche was published in Invent. Math. 189 (2012), not Ann. Sci. ENS. The alpha/beta discrepancy in Bellaiche (5) and the j+1 reading of Pollack-Stevens (2) were confirmed, and each is now backed by a reviewer computation.
